description: OrbitAir is an AI-powered platform that analyzes air quality in Riyadh by combining NASA satellite observations, ground-level pollution measurements, and weather data. Using machine learning and statistical analysis, it identifies spatial and seasonal pollution trends, investigates potential contributing factors, and visualizes findings through interactive maps to support data-driven environmental insights.
summary: Orbit Air is a project that uses NASA satellite data and AI to understand how Riyadh’s air quality has changed over the past 26 years. It helps identify dust and air quality trends, explain what the data tells us, and explore whether we can improve pollution predictions. Our goal is to turn complex environmental data into clear insights that can help build a healthier, smarter future.
details:
Orbit Air is a project that uses NASA satellite data and AI to study how Riyadh's atmosphere has changed over the past 26 years, especially in terms of dust and aerosols.

Our project analyzes satellite observations to identify long-term trends, uses statistical methods to understand how reliable these trends are, and applies Explainable AI to make the results easier to understand. We also tested whether satellite data could improve next-day PM2.5 predictions.

The main benefit of Orbit Air is that it turns complex environmental data into clear insights that can support researchers, environmental agencies, and decision-makers. Our goal is to contribute to better environmental awareness and smarter decisions for a healthier future.

We used NASA MODIS MAIAC data, Python-based data analysis and machine learning, statistical trend tests, and Explainable AI techniques. Our project builds on the modeling and explainability approach we developed in AirSense, which won second place at WiDS PSU 2026.

What makes Orbit Air creative is its combination of long-term satellite observations, AI, and transparent statistical analysis. Instead of simply reporting pollution levels, we investigate how atmospheric conditions change over time and communicate the uncertainty behind our findings.

We also considered data reliability, statistical confidence, limitations of satellite measurements, and the importance of presenting honest results rather than making unsupported claims.
